mood.heading: Mood
mood.lede: A ten-second check-in. Two questions with words you would actually use, and a note if you want one.
mood.formIntro: There is no wrong answer, and you can change any of it before you save.
mood.valenceHint: Pick the closest face. Nothing is measured by it.
mood.energyLegend: How much energy do you have?
mood.energyHint: Move the slider with the arrow keys. The words change with it.
mood.emotionsHint: Up to three words. Skip it if none of them fit.
mood.emotionsFull: That is three. Tap one off to choose a different one.
mood.factorsLegend: What is going on around it? (optional)
mood.factorsHint: Up to five. These are context, not causes.
mood.factorsFull: That is five. Tap one off to choose a different one.
mood.notePlaceholder: A line, a sentence, a fragment. Or nothing at all.
mood.notePrivacy: Stored encrypted, and only ever shown back to you here.
mood.noteOver: That is longer than the note can be. Try shortening it a little.
mood.valenceRequired: Choose the face that is closest. If none of them fit, pick the one you are nearest to.
mood.energyRequired: Choose how much energy you have.
mood.submitHint: Nothing is sent anywhere until you press Save check-in.
mood.errorBody: Your check-in is still on this screen — nothing was lost. Press Save check-in to try again.
mood.errorConsent: This account still needs the data agreements before a check-in can be saved.
mood.savedBody: Thanks for telling me. That is the whole check-in.
mood.savedCrisisLine: Your check-in is saved. You can also look at this:
mood.savedStreakEmpty: Whenever you come back is fine.
mood.crisisSupportHeading: There is support for this, right now
mood.savedActionHeading: One small thing, if it helps
mood.actionFallback: Two slow breaths, with the out-breath longer than the in. That's the whole task.

actions.depleted: Pick the next smallest thing and let the rest wait. A glass of water counts.
actions.sleep: Ten minutes lying down somewhere quiet. Resting counts, even if you do not sleep.
actions.people: One short message to somebody who knows you. It does not have to explain anything.
actions.work: Write down the first line of the thing that is pressing, then stop for now.
actions.money: Write the number down where you can see it. You do not have to solve it this minute.
actions.weather: A minute at a window, or just outside the door, if you can get there.
actions.hardMoment: Put a hand on the table and feel it for a few seconds. Nothing else needs doing.
actions.quietMiddle: Choose one thing and do half of it. Half counts.
actions.ordinary: Name one small thing that went okay today. It can be very small.
actions.goodEnergy: If you have energy to spare, spend ten minutes on something you actually like.
actions.good: Take ten seconds to let this land before you move on.

mood.reminderSaved: Saved on this device. No reminders are sent yet.

mood.historyDeleted: Deleted. Your other check-ins are untouched.

journal.heading: Journal
journal.lede: Write freely. Your title and words are encrypted at rest with your per-user AES-256-GCM key.
journal.crisisHeading: There is support for this, right now
journal.loadError: Could not load your journal entries right now.
journal.saveError: Could not save your reflection right now.
journal.deleteError: Could not delete this journal entry.
journal.loadMoreError: Could not load more journal entries.
journal.privacyBadge: Private by default — AES-256-GCM envelope encryption
journal.privacyIntro1: Every entry’s title and body are encrypted with your per-user 256-bit data key wrapped by
journal.privacyIntro2: , bound to your account ID and column name via Associated Data (AAD) so ciphertexts cannot be swapped.
journal.searchOnlyBody: Because ciphertexts use fresh random 96-bit nonces, the database cannot search inside encrypted entries. Search runs locally in your browser after your entries are fetched.
journal.scoresBody: By default, sentiment and emotion scores are computed in memory when you save and only the numbers are stored in the clear for trend charts. You can turn this off below for any entry.
journal.threatBody1: Because the server wraps and unwraps data keys in memory using
journal.threatBody2: , an attacker who compromises the running application server and reads process memory or environment variables can decrypt entries. This protects against database dumps, SQL injection reads, and disk theft — not a live server compromise.
journal.promptsIntro: Writing prompts (click a chip to use):
journal.editorPlaceholder: Write whatever is on your mind. Changes autosave automatically as you pause typing…
journal.deleteAsk: Delete this reflection permanently? Its ciphertext will be erased from the database and cannot be recovered.
journal.searchEmpty: No entries match your local search.
journal.entriesEmpty: No journal entries yet. Start typing to autosave your first reflection.

templates.freeDescription: An open page with no structure — write whatever is on your mind.

2. Something or someone that made the day a little easier:

templates.worryScaffoldBody:
What is looping in my head right now:
- 

What is actually within my control in the next 24 hours:
- 

What I give myself permission to set down until tomorrow:
-

exercises.lede: One short practice, at your pace. You can pause or stop at any time.
exercises.framing: Self-help, not treatment. Instructions are currently in English. No sound is needed.
exercises.offline: Exercises work offline: once Manovia has loaded on this device, you can open and run them without a connection.
exercises.suggestionsNote: Choose how you feel to see rule-based suggestions. This is not a diagnosis, and your choice is not saved.
exercises.unavailable: Exercises could not be loaded. Please reconnect and try again.

assessments.title: Screenings
assessments.lede: Two short, widely used questionnaires: the PHQ-9 for low mood and the GAD-7 for worry. They are screening tools, not tests you can pass or fail.
assessments.notice: A screening result describes how the last two weeks have been. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not a measure of who you are.
assessments.englishOnly: The questions are shown in English, exactly as published. Officially validated Hindi and Bengali editions will be added when they are sourced; until then nothing here is translated, because a translated screening that was never validated could mislead.

assessments.item9BannerTitle: Before your score, please read this

assessments.trendChartNote: The dashed lines are the questionnaire's band boundaries. The table below has the same numbers.
assessments.provenanceVerbatim: The questions, the answer options and the scoring bands are reproduced exactly as published.
assessments.notADiagnosisFallback: This is a screening result, not a diagnosis. Only a qualified professional can diagnose, and they would do it by talking with you.

assessments.item9Summary: You answered above “Not at all” on the question about thoughts of being better off dead or of hurting yourself. That is why support and helplines were shown first, whatever your total score says.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.lede: What Manovia keeps, what it does not, and how to take it or remove it. Nothing on this page needs a reason or an explanation.
privacy.storageDeviceDetail: Your palette, whether the mood hint is shown, and your sign-in tokens stay in this browser. They are never sent anywhere as preferences.
privacy.storageEncryptedDetail: Journal entries, the messages of chats you chose to save, and any note you attach to a check-in. Each is encrypted with a key that belongs to your account, so it is unreadable at rest without you.
privacy.storageNumbersDetail: Check-in scales (how you rated mood and energy), which tags you picked, and thought-record ratings. These are what make trends possible.
privacy.storageSafetyDetail: When a screening answer is high risk, Manovia records the level, the source and a category — no message text, no journal text, no note. That is why you can delete everything above and the safety record still contains nothing you wrote.
privacy.retentionForever: Keep everything until I delete it.
privacy.saved: Saved. This is what Manovia will do from now on.

privacy.saveErrorGeneric: That choice could not be saved right now. Please try again.

privacy.storeSentimentLabel: Keep mood scores from my writing
privacy.storeSentimentHelp: These are guesses made by a language model, not measurements. Off means new journal entries store no score. Your words are still saved as you wrote them.
privacy.retentionForeverOption: Keep everything until I delete it
privacy.retentionHelp: A cleanup job runs against this window and deletes older entries. Deleting removes them; it does not anonymise them.
privacy.retentionDefaultsNote: Nothing here has been saved yet, so the defaults are showing.
privacy.exportHelp: One file, everything Manovia holds about you, decrypted so you can read it: profile, agreements, saved chats, journal, check-ins, assessments, exercises, thought records, plan and safety events. Keep it somewhere safe — it is unencrypted once downloaded.
privacy.consentsLoadError: Your agreement history could not be loaded right now.
privacy.consentsEmpty: No agreements recorded on this account yet.
privacy.consentsNote: Withdrawing an agreement is not offered here because it does not work like a switch: asking Manovia to stop using your data is what deletion below does. Everything else stays available to you either way.
privacy.anonymousSignedOut: Anonymous accounts carry no email and no password, so nothing here points back at a person. Everything else works exactly the same.
privacy.anonymousActive: You are using an anonymous account: no email, no password, nothing that identifies you. Everything else works the same — the data belongs to this device. The trade-off is that nobody, including you, can recover it if this browser forgets its tokens, so keep a copy of anything you want to keep.
privacy.anonymousEmail: You signed up with an email address, which is the only thing that identifies you. If you would rather not be identifiable, you can delete this account and start again anonymously: everything works the same, and the data then belongs to the device alone.
privacy.anonymousCaveat: Anonymous does not mean invisible: your language, your region and the content you choose to save are still stored as described above, and safety screens still run. It means Manovia holds no name, no email and no phone number that could point back at you.
privacy.deleteHelp: This deletes your account and every row attached to it, in one transaction. It cannot be undone, and it also ends this session — you would come back to a fresh, empty account.
privacy.receiptNote: The reference is a one-way hash, not your account number: it proves the deletion happened without recording who you are.
privacy.passwordHelp: Required because this account signs in with a password.

onboarding.welcomeIntro: A quiet place to notice how you are doing, one small step at a time. Nothing here is shared with anyone else unless you choose to.
onboarding.welcomePoint1: Write about your day, or just sit with a prompt.
onboarding.welcomePoint2: Track your mood and see gentle patterns over time.
onboarding.welcomePoint3: Try short exercises when things feel heavy.
onboarding.welcomeReassurance: You can stop at any point, and you can delete your account and everything in it whenever you want.
onboarding.scopeHeading: What Manovia is — and is not
onboarding.scopeIntro: Being clear about this matters more than any feature, so it comes before anything else.
onboarding.scopeIs1: A self-help companion for everyday ups and downs.
onboarding.scopeIs2: Software that runs on an AI model, with written safety rules around it.
onboarding.scopeIs3: Private by default: your words are encrypted, and never sold.
onboarding.scopeIs4: Yours to control — export, pause, or delete at any time.
onboarding.scopeIsNot1: Not therapy, counselling, or any kind of treatment.
onboarding.scopeIsNot2: Not a diagnosis, and never a substitute for a professional who knows you.
onboarding.scopeIsNot3: Not a crisis service. It cannot send help to you.
onboarding.scopeIsNot4: Not a person. There is no one on the other side reading your messages.
onboarding.aiHeading: Before we start: this is an AI
onboarding.aiIntro: You deserve to know exactly what you are talking to. Here is Manovia's AI disclosure, word for word.
onboarding.aiDisclosure: Manovia is an AI-powered self-help companion. The replies you get are generated by an AI, not written by a human therapist or counsellor. It cannot diagnose you, cannot give medical or medication advice, and is not an emergency or crisis service — if you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a helpline right away. Sharing how you feel can still help you reflect and feel less alone. You are in control: you choose what to write, you can stop at any time, and you can delete your account and its data whenever you want.
onboarding.aiFallbackNote: Manovia could not fetch the current disclosure, so this is the copy shipped with the app.
onboarding.consentNote: Each box is separate and starts unticked. You choose. Only the first three are needed to use Manovia.
onboarding.consentTermsSummary: You are in charge of your account and your entries, you must be old enough to consent in your country, and Manovia is a self-help companion — not therapy, not a diagnosis, and not a crisis service.
onboarding.consentPrivacySummary: What we store (your account, your entries, safety metadata) and why. Chat, journal and mood text is encrypted at rest, is never sold, and can be erased by deleting your account.
onboarding.consentAiSummary: Manovia is software, not a person. What you read here is generated by an AI.
onboarding.consentStoreChatSummary: Optional: let Manovia keep your conversations so you can look back at them. The text is stored encrypted, and withdrawing this consent stops future storage.
onboarding.accountIntro: You can start right now without an email address, or create an account so your entries follow you to another device.
onboarding.passwordHelp: At least 10 characters. Length matters more than symbols.
onboarding.gateError: Manovia needs the three required agreements before you can start.
onboarding.consentHintGranted: You can change these later in Settings.
onboarding.consentHintPending: Tick the three required agreements to continue. The optional one is up to you.
onboarding.footer: Manovia is not a crisis service. If you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a helpline now.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.lede: Manovia should work for everyone who needs it — with a keyboard, a screen reader, zoom, or a slow phone on a weak connection.
a11y.aimBody: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, and go further where it matters for this app: larger tap targets, offline help, and a high-contrast mode.
a11y.do1: Everything works with a keyboard alone, in a logical order, with a visible focus ring and a “Skip to main content” link.
a11y.do2: Pages use headings and landmarks (header, navigation, main, footer), and every page has its own title.
a11y.do3: Every form field has a label; errors are explained in words, linked to the field, and announced.
a11y.do4: Changes that happen without a page load — a reply arriving, a check-in saved, the connection dropping — are announced to screen readers.
a11y.do5: Buttons, links and form controls are at least 44 by 44 pixels; helpline links are at least 48 pixels tall.
a11y.do6: Text follows your browser's font size, and pages reflow without loss at 200% and 400% zoom.
a11y.do7: Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 in both palettes, and at least 7:1 in high-contrast mode. Windows high contrast is supported.
a11y.do8: If your device asks for reduced motion, animations are switched off, including the breathing guide.
a11y.do9: Nothing is timed against you: exercises can be paused at any point, updates wait for you to reload, and nothing signs you out for being slow or offline.
a11y.do10: The app opens offline once it has loaded, so “Need help now?” and the breathing exercises still work without a signal.
a11y.check1: Every screen is scanned with axe-core in a real browser, in light, dark and high-contrast modes, on every change to the code.
a11y.check2: Lighthouse runs on a simulated mid-range phone on a slow 4G connection, with budgets: performance at least 90 and accessibility at least 95.
a11y.check3: Automated keyboard-only walkthroughs go from onboarding to settings, and layouts are checked at 200% and 400% zoom.
a11y.check4: An offline test confirms the helplines, a breathing exercise and a check-in all work with the network switched off.
a11y.limit1: The Hindi and Bengali text is an AI-assisted draft waiting for review by native speakers.
a11y.limit2: Charts on the Insights page have a table view, but the charts themselves are not fully described to screen readers.
a11y.limit3: Exercise instructions, helpline descriptions and the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screenings are in English only for now.
a11y.limit4: Chat needs a connection; it does not work offline.
a11y.limit5: Manovia has not yet been tested with disabled people or audited by an independent accessibility specialist. Automated checks catch many problems, not all of them.
a11y.feedbackBody: If something doesn't work for you, please tell us what you were trying to do and what happened. We read every report.
a11y.feedbackLink: Report an accessibility problem on GitHub
a11y.feedbackPrivacy: Reports there are public. Please don't include anything personal, or anything you have written in Manovia.
